drug_name: Acetaminophen, Dextromethorphan Hydrobromide, Guaifenesin, and Phenylephrine
brand_names: Robitussin Severe Multi-Symptom Cough Cold & Flu
what_its_for: This combination medicine treats multiple cold and flu symptoms at the same time. Acetaminophen reduces fever and relieves pain such as headaches, sore throat, and body aches. Dextromethorphan (often called DXM) helps quiet a dry, nagging cough. Guaifenesin is an expectorant that loosens and thins mucus in your chest so it is easier to cough up. Phenylephrine is a nasal decongestant that shrinks swollen blood vessels in your nose so you can breathe more easily.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with a full glass of water. You may take it with food or milk if it upsets your stomach. If you have a liquid form, use the measuring cup or dosing syringe that comes in the package — do not use a regular kitchen spoon because it may give you the wrong amount. If you have a tablet or caplet, swallow it whole. Drink plenty of fluids (water, broth, or juice) while taking this medicine to help loosen mucus and keep you hydrated.
dosing: Always follow the directions on the package label or your doctor's instructions exactly. For most adults and children 12 years and older, the usual dose is taken every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Do not take more than 4 doses in any 24-hour period. Do not take more than 4,000 mg of acetaminophen (from all sources combined) in one day — check all other medicines you use for acetaminophen because taking too much can seriously harm your liver. For children under 12 years old, check with your doctor or pharmacist before use, as dosing is based on weight and age.
missed_dose: This medicine is usually taken only when you have symptoms and is not taken on a strict schedule. If you are following a scheduled dosing plan and forget a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and take the next one at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time or double up to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store in a bathroom medicine cabinet because heat and humidity can damage the medicine. Keep the bottle or package tightly closed. Keep this and all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the label. Dispose of unused or expired medicine safely — many pharmacies offer take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine. Alcohol increases your risk of liver damage from acetaminophen and can make dizziness or drowsiness worse. Do not drive a car, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you, as it may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Do not take any other medicines that contain acetaminophen (such as other cold, pain, or sleep products) at the same time — doing so can cause a dangerous overdose. Avoid taking this medicine with other cough suppressants, decongestants, or multi-symptom cold products without first checking with your pharmacist. If you take MAO inhibitor antidepressants (such as phenelzine, selegiline, or tranylcypromine), do not take this medicine — wait at least 14 days after stopping an MAO inhibitor before using this product. Avoid caffeine (coffee, energy drinks) as it may increase side effects like nervousness or a fast heartbeat caused by phenylephrine.
when_to_call_doctor: Stop taking this medicine and call your doctor or seek emergency help right away if you notice any of the following: signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing; yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, or severe stomach pain, which could be signs of liver damage; chest pain, fast or irregular heartbeat, or severe dizziness; very high blood pressure symptoms such as a severe headache, blurred vision, or confusion; cough that lasts more than 7 days, keeps coming back, or is accompanied by rash or persistent headache; fever that lasts more than 3 days or rises above 103°F (39.4°C); symptoms that get much worse or do not improve after 7 days. Also call your doctor before using this medicine if you have high blood pressure, heart disease, diabetes, thyroid disease, glaucoma, an enlarged prostate, liver problems, or chronic cough caused by asthma, smoking, or emphysema.
when_it_works: You may start to feel relief from fever, pain, and nasal congestion within 30 to 60 minutes after taking the medicine. The cough suppressant effect usually begins within 15 to 30 minutes. The expectorant (guaifenesin) works gradually over several hours to loosen mucus — be sure to drink plenty of fluids to help it work best. The full effect of each dose typically lasts 4 to 6 hours. This medicine treats your symptoms but does not cure the cold or flu virus itself; most colds improve on their own within 7 to 10 days.
special_populations: PREGNANCY AND BREASTFEEDING: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Phenylephrine and dextromethorphan are generally avoided in the first trimester of pregnancy. Acetaminophen is considered the preferred pain reliever during pregnancy when used as directed, but always check with your healthcare provider first. OLDER ADULTS (65 years and older): You may be more sensitive to the effects of this medicine, especially dizziness, increased blood pressure, and difficulty urinating from phenylephrine. Your doctor may recommend a lower dose or a different product. CHILDREN: Do not give adult-strength products to children under 12 years old. Use only products specifically labeled for your child's age and weight, and always measure doses carefully. Do not give to children under 4 years old unless directed by a doctor. LIVER OR KIDNEY DISEASE: Use with caution and talk to your doctor first — lower doses may be needed, or this medicine may not be appropriate for you. HIGH BLOOD PRESSURE OR HEART DISEASE: The phenylephrine in this medicine can raise blood pressure and heart rate. Check with your doctor before use.
